claim: This project replicates Biswas et al.'s MaxEnt method directly and beats it (0.9576 vs. their 0.879)
evidence_from_audit: Historical MaxEnt (elapid LHP, beta=4, 150k rows, 57 features, pixel presence/absence on 4.16M pixels at 6.5% prevalence, 2000-2022 labels) scores 0.9598 (reproduced; 0.9576 does not appear in any output). Biswas: MaxEnt 3.4.4 presence-background, 15 predictors at 0.25 deg, 2020 presences only, AUC vs background. Populations, predictors, labels, resolution and AUC definition all differ. Biswas-style re-implementation on this project's data under Biswas's protocol gives test AUC 0.893 +/- 0.009 (range 0.877-0.912)
verdict: NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE (and number not traceable)
recommended_wording: Under a Biswas-style protocol re-implemented with this study's data (0.25 deg, 15 level predictors, 2020 presences, MaxEnt), test AUC was 0.893 +/- 0.009 over 10 random presence splits, of the same order as the 0.879 reported by Biswas et al. under their own data. Pixel-level AUCs from this study's 1 km evaluation are not comparable with Biswas et al.'s presence-background AUC.

claim: Full 15/15 predictor-group parity with Biswas et al.
evidence_from_audit: All 15 predictor GROUPS are represented, but in v1 the climate and LST predictors enter only as anomaly-means (degenerate: 26-month out-of-baseline residue) and MK trends; the Biswas-type LEVEL of air temperature, specific humidity, LST, soil moisture, precipitation, wind and net LW is absent from the v1 model. Sources differ for 5 of 15 (LST MOD11A2 vs MOD11C3; NDVI MOD13A3 1 km vs MOD13C2 0.05 deg; precipitation FLDAS/CHIRPS vs GPM IMERG; soil moisture and net LW FLDAS vs GLDAS)
verdict: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (v1) / SUPPORTED at group level (v2)
recommended_wording: All 15 of Biswas et al.'s predictor variables are represented (v2: as 2001-2020 climatological levels, the form Biswas et al. used), five of them from different source products (Table X).

claim: Specific humidity is added beyond Biswas's predictor set / should read 'relative humidity (derived)'
evidence_from_audit: Specific humidity IS one of Biswas's 15 predictors (Table 3), so it is not an extension. In the v1 model, specific humidity enters per pixel (fldas_qair_anomaly, fldas_qair_mk_tau_monthly; 3.76M distinct values) -- the gap document's statement that it is only a national scalar is incorrect. Relative humidity is an ADDITIONAL derived per-pixel predictor
verdict: NOT SUPPORTED (both the manuscript's 'extension' framing and the gap document's proposed correction)
recommended_wording: Specific humidity (FLDAS Qair, the same source Biswas et al. used) enters as a per-pixel predictor; relative humidity derived from specific humidity, air temperature and surface pressure is an additional predictor not used by Biswas et al.

claim: CDR-PINN scores 0.7510 on spatial-block CV versus RF 0.950 and MaxEnt 0.946 'on the same fold scheme' / 'matching CDR-PINN's Track B1 exactly'
evidence_from_audit: Different fold assignment (GroupKFold anchored at 0 deg vs random permutation of blocks anchored at 68.2E/6.75N), different grid (1 km vs 12 km), different label and prevalence (6.5% vs 40.6%), different features (57 vs 7). On CDR-PINO's own cells, folds and covariates, RF scores 0.974 vs CDR-PINO 0.719 (3 seeds)
verdict: NOT SUPPORTED as stated (conclusion direction holds and strengthens)
recommended_wording: On CDR-PINO's own 12 km cells, spatial-block folds and covariates, a Random Forest reached ROC-AUC 0.974 versus 0.719 (mean of 3 seeds) for CDR-PINO.

claim: Temporal generalisation to unseen years is strong (B3 AUC = 0.8960); temporal generalisation no classical baseline was evaluated on
verdict: Reproduced (0.8960; leak-free 0.893 +/- 0.003). On identical cell-months: no-covariate climatological-frequency null 0.908, seasonal-frequency null 0.930, RF with monthly covariates + month 0.972; every CDR-PINO configuration scores below both null baselines
column7: CDR-PINO's leave-years-out AUC (0.893, leak-free) was below that of a covariate-free persistence baseline using each cell's training-period fire frequency (0.908) and seasonal frequency (0.930).

claim: Term ablation demonstrates each mechanism contributes measurable predictive value (diffusion-only 0.602, +advection 0.924, full 0.940)
evidence_from_audit: Historical ablation used a fixed 80-epoch budget without validation, single seed, and no no-physics arm; diffusion-only 0.602 was a documented collapse. Under one validated protocol, 3 seeds: no physics 0.9450, diffusion 0.9242, diff+adv 0.9394, full 0.9388; every physics configuration is significantly BELOW no physics on Track A (DeLong, all seeds) and on B3
recommended_wording: Under an identical validated protocol (3 seeds), no physics-term configuration improved on the same network trained without physics losses; the full CDR model scored 0.006 ROC-AUC lower on the random split and 0.011 lower on unseen years.

claim: Elevation dominates the trained operator; mechanistic attribution capability no correlational baseline offers
verdict: Holds inside the 7-covariate CDR-PINO model. In a model with the full predictor set, removing terrain entirely changes AUC by -0.0001 (all) / -0.0006 (forest) -- terrain is redundant given climate/LST/NDVI. Biswas also rank elevation low (2.4%). Classical permutation importance and jackknife provide the same attribution capability
column7: Within the CDR-PINO covariate set, elevation carries most of the predictive signal; this reflects the restricted covariate set rather than a general driver ranking (with the full predictor set, terrain is redundant).

claim: Each CDR term maps onto Biswas's predictor groups: diffusion<->biophysical/climatic (33.9%+26.1% of their MaxEnt contribution), advection<->topographic (9.7%), reaction<->human (10.8%)
evidence_from_audit: The group totals are Biswas's PERMUTATION IMPORTANCE, not contribution (verified arithmetic). Diffusion term is numerically negligible (0.04% of RHS magnitude) in every trained model; reaction inputs include dryness/NDVI/slope, not only human-activity variables
verdict: NOT SUPPORTED (mislabelled source figures; mapping not reflected in trained dynamics)
recommended_wording: Report group figures as permutation importance; describe the term-to-group mapping as a design intent, and report that the trained diffusion term is numerically negligible.

claim: This extraction runs 0.5-2.4% higher than Biswas et al.'s own annual counts -- a validation
evidence_from_audit: Reproduced: +0.51% to +2.43%, r=0.99996 over 20 years. Biswas counts are derived from rounded percentages x 475,950 (+/-24 points each)
recommended_wording: Annual forest-fire counts agree with those derived from Biswas et al.'s published shares (r = 0.99996; this study 0.5-2.4% higher, 2001-2020).

claim: Pipeline extends Biswas with trend/anomaly/decomposition features
evidence_from_audit: v1 anomaly-means are degenerate; MK trends used invalid tests. With valid Seasonal-Kendall trends, the trend group adds +0.0013 (all) / +0.0056 (forest) AUC (DeLong, identical test set); total extra-predictor gain over Biswas-15 under RF +0.0046 / +0.0123
column7: Additional engineered predictors (valid trend tests, land-cover fractions and others) improved ROC-AUC over the Biswas-equivalent predictor set by 0.005 (all pixels) and 0.012 (forest pixels) under the same model and split.

claim: RF/MaxEnt vs Biswas: this study achieves higher accuracy
evidence_from_audit: Different evaluation population and AUC definition
recommended_wording: Under the present evaluation protocol, the Random Forest achieved 0.975 (all pixels) and 0.897 (forest pixels); Biswas et al. reported 0.879 under a different protocol, population and AUC definition.

claim: Biswas et al. did not validate spatially/temporally; this study adds spatial, regional and temporal validation
evidence_from_audit: Verified: Biswas report only a single random presence hold-out. This study adds spatial-block, regional and unseen-year tracks
verdict: SUPPORTED (as a methodological extension; results must be reported with the nulls)
recommended_wording: This study adds spatial-block, leave-one-region-out and unseen-year evaluation, none of which were reported by Biswas et al.
